title: WebView JavaScript enabled
description: JavaScript is explicitly enabled on a WebView. When combined with loading untrusted content this can lead to script injection.
remediation: Only enable JavaScript when required, restrict navigation to trusted origins, and avoid loading untrusted URLs.

title: WebView JavaScript interface exposed
description: A native object is bridged into WebView JavaScript via addJavascriptInterface. If untrusted content is loaded, exposed methods may be invoked by attacker-controlled script.
remediation: Avoid addJavascriptInterface for untrusted content, annotate only intended methods with @JavascriptInterface, and target API levels where the bridge is restricted.

title: Permissive TrustManager indicator
description: A custom X509TrustManager is implemented. Custom trust managers frequently disable certificate validation; the empty or accept-all case must be verified in the checkServerTrusted body.
remediation: Do not implement custom certificate validation. If required, validate the chain properly and pin certificates rather than accepting all.

title: Permissive hostname verifier indicator
description: A hostname verifier is customized or set to an allow-all implementation, which can defeat TLS hostname checks.
remediation: Use the default hostname verifier and rely on the platform's certificate validation and a network security configuration.

title: Weak cryptographic algorithm indicator
description: A weak or broken cryptographic primitive (MD5, SHA-1, DES/3DES, RC4, or AES in ECB mode) is requested. These do not provide adequate confidentiality or integrity.
remediation: Use SHA-256 or stronger for hashing and AES-GCM (or another authenticated mode) with a random IV for encryption.

title: Hardcoded secret indicator
description: A string that resembles a credential, API key, or token is embedded in the decompiled source. Hardcoded secrets can be recovered by anyone with the APK.
remediation: Remove secrets from the client, rotate any exposed values, and fetch credentials from a secured backend at runtime.
